PC: (chief complaint) “What can I do for you today?” “What brings you to the clinic?” “What made you decide to see a psychiatrist?”
(elaboration of chief complaint) “Can you tell me more about that?” “What kinds of problems have you been having?”
(duration) “How long have you been feeling this way?” “When did these problems first begin?”
(sleep) “Tell me about your sleep.” “How have you been sleeping?” “Have you had any trouble sleeping?”
(diurnal variation) “Is there a time of day that is better or worse?” “Do you feel better in the morning or evening?” “Does your mood change throughout the day?”
(inappropriate guilt/worthlessness) “Have you felt guilty lately? If so, about what?” “Have you been feeling worthless at all?” “How has your self-esteem been?”
(hopelessness) “Have you been feeling hopeless at all?” “What are your plans for the future?” “Do you think things will ever get better?”
(appetite/weight changes) “How has your appetite been lately?” “Have you gained or lost any weight?”
(interest) “What kinds of things do you enjoy doing?” “Are there any activities that bring you pleasure these days?”
(concentration) “Have you noticed any changes in your concentration?” “Have you had any problems reading or focusing on TV shows?” “Are you able to focus on tasks as well as usual?”
(libido) “How is your sex drive?” “Are you still interested in sexual relations?” “Have you noticed any change in your interest in sex?”
(suicidal ideation) “Are you having any thoughts about not wanting to be around?” “Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself?” “Are you thinking about ending your life?”
(suicidal plan) “Have you come up with a plan to harm yourself?” “What ideas have you had about how you might harm yourself?”
(safety clarification) “What exactly do you mean by ‘not really’?” “It sounds like you may have thought about suicide.” “How close have you come to harming yourself?”

(homicidal ideation) “Do you want to take your anger out on other people?” “Are you having any thoughts of harming anyone, like the baby?” “Have you recently gotten so mad that you could kill someone?”

(psychosis) “Have you ever heard voices or seen things other people couldn’t see?” “Have you ever had any unusual experiences?” “Does your mind ever play tricks on you or seem to not be working right?”

(mania) “Do you have times when you are on top of the world and full of energy?” “Have you ever felt excited and energetic for several days in a row?” “Have you ever felt like you could go for days without sleep?”
(alcohol) “Tell me about your use of alcohol.” “How often do you drink alcohol?” “What’s your usual pattern of alcohol use?”
(drugs) “Have you ever used recreational drugs, like marijuana or cocaine?” “Have you ever used street drugs?” “Have you ever experimented with illicit substances?”

(family psychiatric history) “Has anyone in your family suffered from an emotional problem or substance abuse?” “Have any of your blood relatives had a mental illness?” “Has anyone in your family had to see a psychiatrist?”

(father’s treatment) “Did your father receive any treatment [for his mental illness]?” “Was your father ever treated by a doctor for his problems?” “Was your father ever hospitalized in a psychiatric unit?”
(father’s medications) “Was your father ever on any psychiatric medications?” “Do you know what medications your father received?”
(developmental history) “What was it like for you growing up?” “Can you tell me a little bit about your childhood?” “Did you have any difficult experiences as a child?”
ICS: (making an empathic statement) “Going without sleep must be exhausting.” “You sound pretty frustrated.”
